coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Pier 54
record.distance_note: On Terry A. Francois Blvd, within the stretch DataSF's official 'Former San Francisco Redevelopment Agency Project Areas' boundary marks as Mission Bay South, and about 30m from Mission Bay South's own nearest tracked feature (the UCSF Illinois Street Garage/P24 waterfront lawn) -- versus roughly 470m from Mission Rock's own tracked footprint (Pier 48/50). Recorded as adjacent to Mission Bay, not Mission Rock, on that basis. Pier 54 itself predates and is not part of Mission Bay's OCII development program -- it is Port-jurisdiction maritime infrastructure.

record.summary: Pier 54, a Port of San Francisco pier just east of Chase Center and the Mission Bay neighborhood (per SFGate), was red-tagged in early July 2024, according to SFGate. In an August 2024 memo, Port Engineering recommended closing it to the public and tenants for safety reasons, and the 11 tenants were told to vacate by the end of 2024. The Port's draft Five-Year Capital Improvement Program (FY2027-31) proposes $2.0M to demolish the pier's shed; that is a proposed budget line, and no source read says demolition has started or gives a start date.

notes.accuracy_caveat: The outline is Assessor lot 9900054, so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a trace. DataSF lists the pier as its own lot, 9900054 (block 9900, with the pier number as the lot), and the earlier hand trace lies 92% inside it, so the match is clear; no Port document read names the lot. The lot's edge can run a few metres off the visible deck edge, and the lot is the legal boundary, not the deck and shed. Status and use are as shown on this record.

notes.regulatory_context: Red-tagged in early July 2024 (SFGate, Sept 2024); Port Engineering recommended closing the pier to the public and tenants for safety reasons, and its 11 tenants were told to vacate by the end of 2024 (Port memo, Aug 9, 2024, written before that date). The Port's draft Five-Year Capital Improvement Program (FY2027-31, Feb 2026) proposes a 'Pier 54 Shed Demolition' line item totaling $2.0M ($500,000 in FY2026-27 and $1,500,000 in FY2027-28); it is a proposed budget line, no source read says demolition has started, and no line item for full substructure removal appears in that document.

open_questions: No funded plan yet for removing the pier's substructure beyond the shed demolition.

Corrected 2026-10-06 (accuracy audit, October 2026): the closure-announcement milestone was dated December 2024, but the Port's August 9, 2024 memo says formal written notice went to tenants on July 15, 2024 and SFGate reported the closure in September 2024; it is now dated July 15, 2024. The February 2026 draft CIP milestone was flagged expected although the draft was published then; the flag was removed. Corrected 2026-10-12: the map status was 'being removed' and the summary said the pier was 'condemned and closed in 2024'. No source read says removal has begun, and 'condemned' appears in none of them (they say 'red tagged' and close 'for safety reasons'). The status is now 'existing', and the shed demolition appears as an expected milestone from the draft budget line.

Whether the pier closed and its tenants left on the planned end-of-2024 date is not stated by a Port document read. The August 2024 memo and the September 2024 SFGate article were written before that date; the later sources found are a February 2025 public comment that the pier "has recently been vacated" and a February 2026 Port memo that mentions "the Pier 54 shed closure".
Whether the Port adopted the FY2027-31 Five-Year Capital Improvement Program with the Pier 54 shed demolition line unchanged is not confirmed: the document read is a draft (cover: February 2026).

That the Port planned to fence the pier to prevent vandalism is reported only in a search-engine summary of the SFGate article, not independently re-verified here against the full original article text (which sits behind a paywall; the mirror used for this record's other facts may not repeat that detail).

This record's site grouping ("Mission Bay South") reflects DataSF's official redevelopment-project-area boundary, which reaches this stretch of Terry A. Francois Blvd -- not a claim that Pier 54 is a Mission Bay OCII development block, which it is not.

record.notes: Pier 54's outline is Assessor lot 9900054 (see the accuracy note). This is a Port maritime/pier facility, not an OCII Mission Bay South development block -- grouped under the Mission Bay South site here because that is the nearest tracked site and because DataSF's official 'Former San Francisco Redevelopment Agency Project Areas' boundary for Mission Bay South extends north along the Terry A. Francois Blvd shoreline to include this stretch. It is materially farther from Mission Rock's own tracked footprint (Pier 48/50, ~470m away) than from Mission Bay South's nearest tracked features (the UCSF Illinois Street Garage/P24 lawn, ~30m away). Recorded as adjacent rather than tracked because it is Port-jurisdiction maritime infrastructure, not a Mission Bay OCII development parcel like this site's other tracked records. A derelict timber pier stands just north of this footprint, separate from it (probably Pier 52, a separate Port asset; the identification is not confirmed by a source and it is not part of this record).
